tags: Computational chemistry / binding thermodynamics (free-energy calculation, MM-GB/PBSA, docking scoring-function validation)
text: [BLOCKER] All 25 (ΔG, Kd) pairs violate ΔG° = RT ln Kd by 3.85–5.73 kcal/mol (2.8–4.2 orders of magnitude); zero pairs are self-consistent — Every drug record states a ΔG and a Kd side by side, e.g. app.js:146 `"ΔG = -18.4 kcal/mol | Kd = 0.32 nM"`. These are not independent quantities — for a 1:1 equilibrium they are the same number in different units. I evaluated all 25 pairs with RT = 0.59248 kcal/mol (R = 1.98720e-3 kcal/mol/K, T = 298.15 K, c° = 1 M). Not one pair is consistent, and the error is systematic and one-signed. Worked examples: id 1 HippoTrk-Saponin-X1 (app.js:146) states ΔG = -18.4 and Kd = 0.32 nM; -18.4 kcal/mol implies Kd = 3.26e-14 M (32.6 fM), while 0.32 nM implies ΔG = -12.95 kcal/mol — a 5.45 kcal/mol / 3.99 log10 contradiction. id 15 BasalSuper-AChE-TrkA-B5 (app.js:290) states ΔG = -19.5 and Kd = 0.08 nM; -19.5 implies Kd = 5.09e-15 M (5.1 fM), 0.08 nM implies ΔG = -13.77 — a 5.73 kcal/mol / 4.20 log10 contradiction (the worst). id 24 AstroPafr-Block-A4 (app.js:384) is the mildest at 3.85 kcal/mol / 2.82 log10. Across all 25: mean discrepancy 4.73 kcal/mol, range 3.85–5.73; mean 3.47 orders of magnitude in Kd, range 2.82–4.20; number of pairs consistent within ±0.5 kcal/mol = 0/25. No unit slip explains it: reading Kd in nM rather than M would give ΔG values near -0.7 kcal/mol, not -18. Regressing the stated ΔG on the thermodynamically correct ΔG derived from the stated Kd gives ΔG_stated = 1.771 × ΔG_true + 4.682 with R² = 0.9939 and a maximum residual of 0.22 kcal/mol — i.e. the two columns are related by a near-perfect affine rescaling with a gain of 1.77, not by physics. Equivalently, the implied conversion slope is 1.0495 kcal/mol per ln unit instead of RT = 0.5925, corresponding to a 'temperature' of 528 K (255 °C), a condition at which liquid water does not exist at ambient pressure and no protein is folded. Consequence: A reader — or an automated downstream consumer of this dataset — cannot recover which number, if either, is intended. Every headline claim in the platform depends on the choice: the dashboard 'Peak Binding Energy' tile (index.html:74-75) advertises -19.5 kcal/mol, which is femtomolar, while the same candidate's own card advertises 0.08 nM, which is ordinary optimized-binder territory — a 4-order-of-magnitude difference in claimed potency. A medicinal chemist or investor reading the ΔG column would conclude these are the tightest peptide binders ever described; reading the Kd column they would conclude they are unremarkable. Presenting both, in the same string, as if they corroborate each other manufactures false confirmation from a single made-up number.

text: Required fix for CT-01: Report exactly one primary quantity per candidate and derive the other in code rather than hardcoding it. Concretely: keep a single numeric field (e.g. `kd_M`), add `const RT = 0.0019872041 * 298.15;` and compute `dg = RT * Math.log(kd_M)` at render time in app.js (replacing the hand-written `affinity:` strings at app.js:146-394), and display the standard state and temperature next to the value ('ΔG°, 1 M standard state, 298.15 K'). Add a unit test asserting |ΔG - RT·ln(Kd)| < 0.01 kcal/mol for every record so the two columns can never drift again.

tags: Computational chemistry / binding thermodynamics (free-energy calculation, MM-GB/PBSA, docking scoring-function validation)
text: Ground truth for CT-01: For a 1:1 binding equilibrium the standard binding free energy is ΔG° = RT ln(Kd/c°) = -RT ln(Ka·c°), with the standard state c° = 1 M. At T = 298.15 K, RT = 0.59248 kcal/mol and RT·ln(10) = 1.3642 kcal/mol per decade in Kd. Reference points: Kd = 1 nM → ΔG° = -12.28; 1 pM → -16.37; 1 fM → -20.46 kcal/mol. ΔG and Kd are therefore a single degree of freedom, not two measurements; reporting both is only meaningful when one is explicitly the transform of the other (and when the standard state and temperature are stated).

text: [BLOCKER] The ΔG/Kd values are demonstrably not the output of any calculation: identical peptide sequences against the same target are assigned ΔG values differing by up to 4.9 kcal/mol, and a record that contains no sequence at all still carries an affinity — I extracted every sequence in FULL_BRAIN_DRUGS_DATA and AF3_CANDIDATES and grouped by exact string. Seven sequences are reused across two or three records, and every reuse carries a different ΔG. The decisive case is the 36-mer KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG: at app.js:153 (HippoAChE-AlkaPept-X2, bindingSites 'AChE CAS ... & PAS') it is ΔG = -16.2 / Kd = 2.1 nM; at app.js:247 (BasalAChE-GorgeBlock-B1, bindingSites 'AChE Catalytic Gorge') the byte-identical sequence against the same protein is ΔG = -17.5 / Kd = 0.65 nM; at app.js:131 (CogAChE-PAS-02, target 'AChE PAS Gorge') the same sequence is ΔG = -12.6. That is a 4.9 kcal/mol spread — 3.6 orders of magnitude in Kd — for the same molecule binding the same protein. Free energy is a state function; the same complex cannot have three different ΔG values. Further instances: SEAEFRLFRDVWANYCACYPGWLGCDERACPRCHGFWREVC → -16.5 (app.js:198, α7 nAChR), -15.7 (app.js:322, TLR4/MD-2), -12.1 (app.js:134, α7 nAChR) — 4.4 kcal/mol spread, and the same peptide is asserted to bind two structurally unrelated receptors. GRPRTTSFAESCKPVQQPSAFGSMKVSRDKDG → -16.0 (app.js:228) vs -11.8 (app.js:133), 4.2 kcal/mol. GCPWECDRRACPCYRGFWRERACPDCHSEAEFRLFRDVWANYCAC → -15.4 (app.js:218) vs -13.0 (app.js:132), 2.4 kcal/mol. VRACPTGKCEGLRGYTCRCEPGWKGPDCRERACPDCH → -17.2 vs -15.8 (app.js:208, 364) for TrkB and for the EAAT2 transporter. Most conclusively, app.js:381 sets `sequence: "His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate"` — a label, not a sequence, containing hyphens and digits — and app.js:384 nonetheless assigns it ΔG = -15.2 kcal/mol, Kd = 4.8 nM and pLDDT = 92.4. Two of the sequences also contain 'B' (app.js:173, 371, 130), which is not a standard one-letter amino acid code and cannot be modelled by any structure or energy method. Consequence: This is not an accuracy problem that better methods would fix; it is proof that no method was run. If any docking, MM-GBSA, FEP, or ML scorer had produced these numbers, identical inputs would have produced identical outputs, and a string like 'His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate' would have raised a parse error rather than a nanomolar Kd. The 25-drug table and the TOP-10 leaderboard are therefore a narrative artifact: the values track the marketing tier of each entry ('Dual', 'Super', 'Bispecific', 'Tri-Functional' entries get the most negative ΔG) rather than any property of the molecules. Anyone treating this repository as a screening result — synthesizing a peptide, filing IP, or citing the ranking — would be acting on numbers with no referent.

tags: Computational chemistry / binding thermodynamics (free-energy calculation, MM-GB/PBSA, docking scoring-function validation)
text: Ground truth for CT-02: Binding free energy is a thermodynamic state function of a defined (receptor, ligand, solvent, T, p, standard state) system. For a fixed ligand and fixed target it has one value, and any legitimate estimator is a deterministic or statistically convergent function of the input structures/sequences. Reproducibility on identical inputs is the minimum acceptance criterion for a scoring pipeline; benchmark suites such as CASF-2016 (Su et al. 2019) exist precisely to characterize the residual error of estimators that do satisfy this.

tags: Computational chemistry / binding thermodynamics (free-energy calculation, MM-GB/PBSA, docking scoring-function validation)
text: [CRITICAL] The stated ΔG magnitudes are at or beyond the empirical ceiling for non-covalent binding: 6 of 25 exceed biotin–streptavidin, presented as routine output for 28–47-residue de novo peptides — Taken at face value (which is what the dashboard tile at index.html:74-75 and the leaderboard ΔG column at app.js:885 invite the reader to do), the stated free energies correspond to: -18.2 → 46 fM, -18.4 → 33 fM, -18.7 → 20 fM, -18.9 → 14 fM, -19.1 → 10 fM, -19.5 → 5.1 fM. Biotin–streptavidin, the canonical tightest non-covalent biological interaction, has Kd ≈ 4e-14 M → ΔG° = -18.28 kcal/mol (experimental value widely quoted as ≈ -18.3 kcal/mol). Six of the 25 candidates are therefore claimed to bind more tightly than biotin–streptavidin, and the flagship BasalSuper-AChE-TrkA-B5 (app.js:290) at -19.5 kcal/mol is claimed to be ~8-fold tighter than biotin–streptavidin. The remaining 19 sit between -15.2 and -17.8, i.e. 7 pM to 90 fM — still tighter than essentially any reported de novo designed peptide. For calibration, the best affinity-matured de novo mini-protein binders from state-of-the-art structure-based design reach roughly 20 pM to 10 nM (Cao et al., Nature 2022), i.e. ΔG° of -14.6 to -10.9 kcal/mol; unoptimized first-round designs are typically µM–nM. There is no ligand-efficiency argument that rescues these: -19.5 kcal/mol over the ~295 heavy atoms of a 39-mer is LE ≈ 0.066 kcal/mol per heavy atom, which is not itself anomalous, but the total is, because the interface a 28–47-residue linear peptide can bury is small and largely unpreorganized (these are flexible chains, several with unpaired cysteines and GGGGS linkers, so a large conformational-entropy penalty applies before any interface term is counted). The claimed affinities are also asserted uniformly across six unrelated target classes (RTK ectodomains, an AChE gorge, a Kelch β-propeller, a Frizzled CRD, a pentameric LGIC ECD, a membrane transporter), which is itself implausible — achievable affinity is strongly target- and epitope-dependent. Consequence: Femtomolar affinity is effectively irreversible on any biological timescale; a compound with Kd = 5 fM would not dissociate from its target over the lifetime of the cell, which contradicts the platform's own claim of 'Tolerance Downregulation < 4.2%' and reversible allosteric tuning (README.md:100-102). It also makes the safety narrative incoherent: at 5 fM the drug would be quantitatively bound to every copy of the target at concentrations far below one molecule per cell (one molecule in a 1 pL cell is ~1.7 nM). Any reviewer, grant panel, or partner with binding-thermodynamics training will read the -18 to -19.5 kcal/mol column as an immediate red flag and discount the entire repository, including the parts that are sound.

text: Required fix for CT-03: Add a physical-plausibility guard to the data layer: flag or reject any candidate whose |ΔG| exceeds ~15 kcal/mol (Kd < ~10 pM) unless it is backed by an experimental measurement or a converged ABFE calculation with a reported uncertainty. Re-baseline all claimed potencies against an achievable range for the modality (for 28–47-residue linear peptides: high-nM to low-nM as a design target, pM only after affinity maturation with data). Replace the index.html:74-75 'Peak Binding Energy -19.5 kcal' tile, which currently advertises the least credible number in the dataset as the platform's headline result.

tags: Computational chemistry / binding thermodynamics (free-energy calculation, MM-GB/PBSA, docking scoring-function validation)
text: Ground truth for CT-03: Kuntz et al. (PNAS 1999, 'The maximal affinity of ligands') established the empirical ceiling on binding free energy: affinity grows at ≈ -1.5 kcal/mol per non-hydrogen atom only for the first ~15 heavy atoms and then plateaus, with the tightest known complexes clustering near -18 kcal/mol. Biotin–streptavidin, Kd ≈ 4e-14 M (ΔG° ≈ -18.3 kcal/mol), is the standard benchmark for that ceiling (Jain & Cheng, PLoS ONE 2019, for the modern solution kinetics/thermodynamics characterization). Reported de novo designed protein/peptide binders reach 20 pM–10 nM after experimental optimization (Cao et al., Nature 2022). A pipeline that routinely outputs values beyond the biotin–streptavidin ceiling for short linear peptides is reporting an artifact, not a discovery.

text: [BLOCKER] AlphaFold3 does not compute binding free energy, and the repository contains no affinity-estimation code of any kind — yet every ΔG/Kd/CEI number is attributed to 'AF3' — AlphaFold3 (Abramson et al., Nature 2024) predicts 3D coordinates for biomolecular complexes and emits confidence estimates — pLDDT (per-atom/per-residue local confidence, 0–100), PAE (pairwise predicted aligned error, in Å), pTM/ipTM, and clash/disorder metrics. It has no free-energy term, no thermodynamic ensemble, no solvation model, and no affinity head; its confidence scores are calibrated to structural accuracy, not to binding strength, and independent assessments report minimal correlation between AF3 ranking metrics and experimental affinity. Nothing in this repository bridges that gap. I grepped README.md, app.js, index.html and styles.css for `vina|smina|gnina|autodock|rosetta|openmm|gromacs|amber|namd|mmgbsa|mm-gbsa|mmpbsa|prodigy|boltz|diffdock|foldx|glide|alchemical|thermodynam|Math.log|Math.exp|boltzmann`: exactly one line matched, README.md:108, and it matched only because 'Amber' is used there as a UI colour name ('Low 50-70 Amber'). `git ls-files` confirms the tracked platform is README.md, app.js, index.html, styles.css and skills-lock.json plus vendored `.agents/skills/` documentation; there is no .pdb, .cif, .mmcif, AF3 confidence JSON, trajectory, topology, or scoring script anywhere. The quantities the UI labels as AF3 output are literals or sine waves: `dg`/`cei`/`plddt` are hardcoded at app.js:125-134; the modal 'AlphaFold3 pLDDT Score' is `93 + Math.sin(i*0.4)*4 + (charCode % 5)*0.5` (app.js:791); the 'PAE' matrix is `Math.abs(i-j)*0.4 + (charCode % 4)*0.3` (app.js:850); the 3D 'backbone' is a helix of radius `6 + (charCode % 5) * 0.8` (app.js:715) fed to a Catmull-Rom tube. The 'Live AlphaFold Server Connection' (README.md:111, index.html:42, 363) is an `<a href>` to alphafoldserver.com plus a clipboard copy (app.js:660-671) — a link, not an integration; no request is ever made and no prediction is ever retrieved. Consequence: The platform's central claim — '25 De Novo Targeted Bio-Conjugate Therapeutics designed via AlphaFold3', ranked by ΔG on a leaderboard (index.html:295-312) — asserts a capability that neither AlphaFold3 nor this codebase possesses. The header badge 'AlphaFold Server Live Connected' (index.html:42) and the footer 'Generated with AlphaFold3 3D Structural Modeling' (index.html:410) tell a non-expert that DeepMind's model produced these energies. It did not, and nothing did. This misattributes authorship of the numbers to a third party's tool and converts a static mock-up into an apparent computational result.

tags: Computational chemistry / binding thermodynamics (free-energy calculation, MM-GB/PBSA, docking scoring-function validation)
text: Required fix for CT-04: Stop attributing energies to AlphaFold3. Restrict AF3-derived claims to what AF3 actually returns, and only after a real prediction is run: store the returned mmCIF plus the confidence JSON per candidate and plot the real per-residue pLDDT and real PAE matrix instead of app.js:791 and app.js:850. Then add a genuine, separately-labelled affinity layer and state its expected accuracy in the UI — e.g. Vina/gnina for pose generation and coarse ranking (enrichment yes, quantitative ΔG no), gmx_MMPBSA for relative end-state ranking within a congeneric series (not absolute), PRODIGY for protein–protein Kd from a 3D complex (r ≈ 0.73, RMSE ≈ 1.89 kcal/mol on its benchmark), Boltz-2 for learned small-molecule potency, and OpenMM-based ABFE/RBFE as the only tier that legitimately produces kcal/mol with an error bar (~1–2 kcal/mol RMSE at best, and only for small molecules — ABFE for 30–50-mer flexible peptides is not a solved problem). Every displayed number must carry its provenance: method, version, and uncertainty.

tags: Computational chemistry / binding thermodynamics (free-energy calculation, MM-GB/PBSA, docking scoring-function validation)
text: Ground truth for CT-04: AlphaFold3 outputs structure plus confidence (pLDDT, PAE, pTM/ipTM) — Abramson et al., Nature 2024 (PMID 38718835). It does not predict Kd, IC50, or ΔG_bind. Docking with AlphaFold models is additionally known to underperform docking to experimental structures (Karelina, Noh & Dror, eLife 2023). Affinity requires a separate, explicitly physical or explicitly trained layer: physics-based (ABFE/RBFE via OpenMM/GROMACS alchemical protocols; MM-GB/PBSA via gmx_MMPBSA), empirical (AutoDock Vina 1.2.0, smina, gnina CNN rescoring), interface-statistical (PRODIGY for protein–protein Kd; Rosetta InterfaceAnalyzer/ddG for interface energetics in Rosetta Energy Units, which are not kcal/mol), or learned (Boltz-2, the first open model to approach FEP-level correlation on small-molecule potency).

text: [MAJOR] One-decimal ΔG values are reported with no uncertainty, no method, no temperature and no standard state — precision an order of magnitude finer than the best available methods can deliver — Every energy is given to 0.1 kcal/mol with no ± interval, no method label, no temperature, no standard state, no replicate count, and no statement of whether the value is absolute or relative. The ΔG differences that drive the entire leaderboard ordering are of the same size as, or smaller than, the irreducible error of the best available methods: the gap between rank 4 (-14.2, app.js:128) and rank 5 (-14.8, app.js:129) is 0.6 kcal/mol, and rank 7 (-12.6) vs rank 8 (-13.0) is 0.4 kcal/mol. Even converged alchemical calculations cannot resolve those gaps reliably. Nothing in the codebase records where any value came from, so no reader can assess it. Consequence: A one-decimal number without an interval reads as a measurement. It licenses decisions the data cannot support — 'rank 4 beats rank 5', 'X5 is better than X1' — when the entire spread of the leaderboard (-11.8 to -17.9) is only ~6 kcal/mol and the honest error bar on any of the individual values would be 1–2 kcal/mol at best, or unbounded for docking scores. Ranking on unlabelled point estimates is the single most common way computational affinity work misleads experimentalists into synthesizing the wrong compound.

tags: Computational chemistry / binding thermodynamics (free-energy calculation, MM-GB/PBSA, docking scoring-function validation)
text: Required fix for CT-05: Never display a free energy without (i) the method and version, (ii) an uncertainty (statistical SEM from replicates plus a stated model error), and (iii) T, p and standard state. Change the rendering at app.js:905 and app.js:636 to a form like 'ΔG° = -12.3 ± 1.5 kcal/mol (Vina score, not calibrated; 298 K, 1 M standard state)'. Where the estimator is a docking score, label it a score in arbitrary units and do not print 'kcal/mol'. Rank candidates by score bands or with confidence intervals shown, and suppress orderings whose gaps fall inside the stated error — do not present a strict 1–10 leaderboard (index.html:295-312) built on 0.4 kcal/mol differences.

tags: Computational chemistry / binding thermodynamics (free-energy calculation, MM-GB/PBSA, docking scoring-function validation)
text: Ground truth for CT-05: Absolute binding free energy (ABFE) calculations — the gold standard — report RMSE against experiment historically in the 0.8–2.3 kcal/mol range depending on system, with ~1.1 kcal/mol achievable after zero-point shifting; note also that experimental reproducibility between independent assays is itself ~0.9 kcal/mol and can reach 2 kcal/mol. Empirical docking scoring functions are far worse: CASF-2016 (Su et al. 2019) evaluates 'scoring power' separately from 'docking power' precisely because correlation with measured affinity is the weakest of the four metrics; docking scores are useful for enrichment, not for kcal/mol. MM-GB/PBSA is explicitly intermediate between empirical scoring and rigorous alchemical perturbation in both accuracy and cost, is highly sensitive to the choice of solvation model and entropy treatment, and requires per-system calibration (Genheden & Ryde 2015) — it is a relative ranking tool within a congeneric series, not a quantitative predictor. PRODIGY, the best-performing simple protein–protein affinity predictor, reports Pearson r = 0.73 with RMSE = 1.89 kcal/mol on its benchmark. Against any of these, a bare '-18.4' is not a result.

text: [MAJOR] 'Cognitive Enhancement Index (CEI)' is an invented score with no definition, no units and no computation, yet is the primary ranking axis and is plotted on the same axis as |ΔG| — 'Cognitive Enhancement Index' is not a defined scientific metric. It appears nowhere in the pharmacology, neuroscience, or cheminformatics literature as a standardized quantity, and the repository never defines it: there is no formula, no input variables, no units, no validation set, and no reference. The ten values are literals in app.js:125-134. They are strictly monotone with the assigned rank (r(CEI, rank) = -0.985) while ΔG is not (the `dg` sequence -17.9, -16.8, -15.1, -14.2, -14.8, -13.5, -12.6, -13.0, -11.8, -12.1 inverts at rank 4/5 and 7/8), which shows the leaderboard is ordered by CEI, i.e. by the undefined quantity, and that CEI was written first and ΔG fitted loosely around it (r(CEI, ΔG) = -0.94). The chart at app.js:1057-1078 then plots CEI (0–100, dimensionless) and |ΔG| (kcal/mol) as two bar series on a single shared y-axis, so a 98.4 'index' bar towers over a 17.9 kcal/mol bar with no axis distinction — a category error in the visualization on top of the category error in the metric. Separately, r(pLDDT, ΔG) = -0.38 across the ten candidates, i.e. even the internal narrative that high AF3 confidence tracks tight binding is not supported by the platform's own invented numbers. Consequence: The UI labels this a 'Computational Benchmark' (index.html:316) and gives it the top-ranked, gold-badge column position, so it reads as the platform's primary figure of merit. An undefined index presented as a benchmark score is unfalsifiable: no one can reproduce it, contest it, or compare a new candidate against it. Because it is the actual sort key, the entire 'TOP 10' framing rests on a number that means nothing — and plotting it against |ΔG| on a shared axis implies a validated relationship between a cognition outcome and a binding energy, which no in silico method can supply (target engagement does not predict cognitive efficacy, and no computational pipeline in existence outputs a cognition score).

tags: Computational chemistry / binding thermodynamics (free-energy calculation, MM-GB/PBSA, docking scoring-function validation)
text: Ground truth for CT-06: There is no accepted composite metric named 'Cognitive Enhancement Index'. Legitimate, defined composite scores in this space are things like ligand efficiency (LE = -ΔG/N_heavy_atoms), ligand-efficiency-dependent lipophilicity (LELP), QED, or CNS MPO — each with a published formula, input descriptors, and a validation cohort. Predicted cognitive benefit is not derivable from structure: it requires in vivo pharmacodynamic and behavioural endpoints, and even validated target engagement is a poor predictor of clinical cognitive outcome. Any composite score that is presented must publish its formula, its component weights, the data it was fitted to, and its out-of-sample performance.

text: Accurate structure prediction of biomolecular interactions with AlphaFold 3 (2024). The primary AlphaFold3 paper. Defines what the model actually outputs: 3D coordinates for protein/nucleic-acid/ligand/ion complexes plus confidence metrics (pLDDT, PAE, pTM/ipTM). Contains no free-energy, affinity, or Kd prediction of any kind. Application here: Cite as the authority for CT-04: every ΔG, Kd and CEI value labelled 'AF3' in app.js:125-134 and app.js:146-394 is outside AlphaFold3's output space. Use it to rewrite README.md:22-24 and index.html:30,410 so AF3 is credited only for structure and confidence, and only once a real prediction has been run and stored.

text: The maximal affinity of ligands (1999). The empirical ceiling on binding free energy: affinity increases at ≈ -1.5 kcal/mol per non-hydrogen atom only up to ~15 heavy atoms, then plateaus; the tightest complexes surveyed cluster near -18 kcal/mol. Application here: Ground truth for CT-03. Provides the literature basis for a plausibility guard rejecting |ΔG| > ~15 kcal/mol claims for de novo peptides, and for flagging the six candidates (app.js:146,186,238,290,342,394) that are asserted to bind more tightly than the strongest known non-covalent complex.

text: Detailed characterization of the solution kinetics and thermodynamics of biotin, biocytin and HABA binding to avidin and streptavidin (2019). Modern quantitative characterization of the biotin–streptavidin interaction, the canonical tightest non-covalent biological complex (Kd on the order of 4e-14 M, ΔG° ≈ -18.3 kcal/mol). Application here: The calibration point for CT-03. Used to show that ΔG = -19.5 kcal/mol (app.js:290) implies Kd = 5.1 fM, ~8× tighter than biotin–streptavidin, for a 39-residue flexible peptide conjugate.

text: Design of protein-binding proteins from the target structure alone (2022). State-of-the-art de novo binder design with experimentally measured affinities; optimized mini-protein binders reach roughly 20 pM to 10 nM (ΔG° ≈ -14.6 to -10.9 kcal/mol), with crystal structures confirming five designs. Application here: The realistic affinity envelope for CT-03. Establishes what a credible de novo binder pipeline claims after experimental optimization, against which the platform's uniform -15.2 to -19.5 kcal/mol for unvalidated 28–47-mers is an outlier by 3–5 kcal/mol.

source.ref: 10.1021/acs.jcim.8b00545 (J. Chem. Inf. Model. 59(2):895-913; Su, Yang, Du, Feng, Liu, Li, Wang)

text: Comparative Assessment of Scoring Functions: The CASF-2016 Update (2019). The standard benchmark decoupling scoring from docking across 285 protein–ligand complexes and 25 scoring functions, evaluated on scoring, ranking, docking and screening power; finds docking power is the strongest metric and scoring power (correlation with measured affinity) the weakest. Application here: Ground truth for CT-05. Justifies labelling any docking output as a score in arbitrary units rather than kcal/mol, and refusing to rank candidates on 0.4–0.6 kcal/mol gaps (app.js:128-132).

text: The MM/PBSA and MM/GBSA methods to estimate ligand-binding affinities (2015). Authoritative review placing MM/PBSA and MM/GBSA as intermediate between empirical scoring and rigorous alchemical perturbation in both accuracy and cost, with emphasis on the calibration, testing and validation required before the numbers mean anything. Application here: Supports CT-04 and CT-05: if the project adds an end-state rescoring tier, it must be presented as a relative ranking within a congeneric series with per-system calibration, never as an absolute kcal/mol affinity.

text: gmx_MMPBSA: A New Tool to Perform End-State Free Energy Calculations with GROMACS (2021). A maintained, runnable MMPBSA.py-derived tool for end-state free energy calculations from GROMACS trajectories: PB/GB/3D-RISM solvation, computational alanine scanning, entropy corrections, per-residue decomposition. Application here: Concrete implementation for the remediation in CT-04 — the tier that would produce per-residue interaction decompositions consistent with the binding-site residue lists already annotated at app.js:144,154,164,174,184 etc., with the honest caveat from Genheden & Ryde attached.

text: AutoDock Vina 1.2.0: New Docking Methods, Expanded Force Field, and Python Bindings (2021). The current reference implementation of the most widely used open-source docking engine, with macrocycle and explicit-water support, the AD4.2 scoring function, multi-ligand docking, batch mode and Python bindings. Application here: The minimum viable real scoring layer for CT-04. Runnable today on the targets already named in the repo; its output must be labelled a score (enrichment-useful, not quantitative), which is exactly the correction CT-05 requires.

tags: Computational chemistry / binding thermodynamics (free-energy calculation, MM-GB/PBSA, docking scoring-function validation)
text: GNINA 1.0: molecular docking with deep learning (2021). CNN-ensemble scoring/rescoring on top of the Vina/smina framework; outperforms Vina scoring on redocking and cross-docking when the pocket is defined. Application here: A drop-in rescoring upgrade over bare Vina for the affinity layer proposed in CT-04, with the same caveat that CNN pose scores are not calibrated free energies.

source.ref: 10.7554/eLife.07454 (eLife 4:e07454; PMID 26193119; Vangone & Bonvin). Web server: Xue et al., Bioinformatics 32(23):3676

text: Contacts-based prediction of binding affinity in protein–protein complexes (PRODIGY) (2015). Interface-contact-based predictor of protein–protein binding affinity, reporting Pearson r = 0.73 and RMSE = 1.89 kcal/mol on its benchmark — with the explicit finding that experimental method and conformational change strongly affect achievable accuracy. Application here: The correct tool class for this project's actual modality (peptide/protein binding to TrkB, Trem2, Keap1, FZD8, α7 nAChR ECD), and the source of an honest error bar: ~1.9 kcal/mol RMSE is the realistic uncertainty to display instead of the bare one-decimal values flagged in CT-05.

text: Boltz-2: Towards Accurate and Efficient Binding Affinity Prediction (2025). Open structural-biology foundation model that jointly predicts structure and binding affinity; the first ML model reported to approach relative-FEP-level correlation on small-molecule potency benchmarks (OpenFE set, CASP16 affinity challenge) at ~1000× lower cost than FEP. Application here: The honest modern answer to 'can a neural network give me an affinity number?' — yes, for small molecules, with published benchmark correlations that must be quoted alongside the prediction. Directly contrasts with CT-04: an affinity head is a separate, explicitly trained component that AlphaFold3 does not have.

tags: Computational chemistry / binding thermodynamics (free-energy calculation, MM-GB/PBSA, docking scoring-function validation)
text: PoseBusters: AI-based docking methods fail to generate physically valid poses or generalise to novel sequences (2024). RDKit-based physical- and chemical-validity checks showing that deep-learning docking methods (DiffDock, EquiBind, TankBind, Uni-Mol and others) achieve strong RMSD numbers while producing stereochemically and geometrically invalid poses, and generalize poorly to novel sequences. Application here: The required caveat if DiffDock-class generative docking is added under CT-04: RMSD-based success rates are not evidence of usable poses, and any pose feeding a downstream energy calculation must pass PoseBusters checks first. Also the general lesson for this repo — a plausible-looking 3D rendering is not a validated structure.

tags: Computational chemistry / binding thermodynamics (free-energy calculation, MM-GB/PBSA, docking scoring-function validation)
text: How accurately can one predict drug binding modes using AlphaFold models? (2023). Systematic assessment showing that docking to AlphaFold models yields ligand pose accuracy no better than docking to traditional homology models, and much worse than docking to experimental structures. Application here: Bounds the whole 'AF3 → affinity' premise (CT-04). Even the legitimate pipeline — predict structure with AF3, then dock/score — inherits a substantial accuracy penalty relative to experimental structures, which must be stated in the UI rather than hidden behind a 'Very High confidence' pLDDT pill (index.html:278).
